title: An introduction to organic chemistry
objectives: Interpret and use general, structural, displayed and skeletal formulae, and deduce molecular and empirical formulae
Understand and use systematic (IUPAC) nomenclature for the homologous series in the syllabus, and recognise their functional groups
Classify alcohols, halogenoalkanes and amines as primary, secondary or tertiary
Describe the shapes of organic molecules using sp³ and sp² hybridisation and σ and π bonds
Understand the terms homolytic and heterolytic fission, free radical, nucleophile, electrophile, and addition, substitution, elimination, hydrolysis, condensation, oxidation and reduction
Describe structural isomerism (chain, positional, functional group) and stereoisomerism (geometrical and optical), identify chiral centres and deduce the number of isomers
prior: Covalent bonding, σ and π bonds, hybridisation and shapes (Chapter 3)
why: Organic chemistry makes up nearly half of the AS papers. Before learning reactions you need the language: how to write and read formulae, name compounds, describe how bonds break and what kinds of reagent attack, and count isomers. Isomerism questions alone appear several times on every Paper 1.
intro: Organic compounds are based on chains and rings of carbon atoms. A homologous series is a family with the same functional group and general formula, in which each member differs by CH₂. This chapter covers formulae, naming, the vocabulary of mechanisms and the different kinds of isomerism.

blocks.h: For alcohols and halogenoalkanes, count the carbon atoms attached to the carbon that carries the OH or halogen: one → primary, two → secondary, three → tertiary.

In ethene each carbon uses three sp² orbitals for σ bonds, and the remaining p orbitals overlap sideways to form a π bond above and below the plane. The π bond stops rotation about the C=C, which is why alkenes can have geometrical isomers.

blocks.q: How many sp³ carbon atoms are there in but-1-ene, CH₂=CHCH₂CH₃?
blocks.why: The two C=C carbons are sp²; the CH₂ and CH₃ are sp³.

blocks.h: Curly arrows show the movement of a pair of electrons, from a lone pair or a bond to an atom or a new bond. Half-headed arrows (fish-hooks) show single electrons in radical reactions.
Compounds with the same molecular formula but different structural formulae.

blocks.name: isomers
blocks.title: Isomer explorer
blocks.h: Choose a formula to list its structural isomers, with notes on which ones also have stereoisomers.
Compounds with the same structural formula but a different arrangement of atoms in space.
Needs (1) restricted rotation about a C=C (the π bond) and (2) two different groups on each carbon of the C=C. Cis: the same groups on the same side; trans: on opposite sides.
A carbon atom bonded to four different atoms or groups.

A molecule with one chiral centre exists as two optical isomers (enantiomers): non-superimposable mirror images. They rotate plane-polarised light in opposite directions. Draw them in 3D with wedges and dashes, as mirror images.

blocks.name: chiral
blocks.title: Chiral centre hunter
blocks.h: Tap each carbon that is a chiral centre and check your answer. Remember: four different groups.
Each C=C that can show cis/trans and each chiral centre doubles the number: number of stereoisomers = 2ⁿ, where n is the number of such features (for the molecules met at AS).

blocks.q: How many stereoisomers does CH₃CH=CHCH(OH)CH₃ have?
steps: C=C: H and CH₃ on one carbon, H and CH(OH)CH₃ on the other → cis/trans
CH(OH): H, OH, CH₃, CH=CHCH₃ → chiral
blocks.err: Adding (2 + 2 = 4 works here by luck) instead of multiplying; with three features it is 8, not 6.

blocks.wrong: Every carbon with four groups attached is chiral.
blocks.right: The four groups must all be different. Look for two identical CH₃ groups or two H atoms.

summary: Formulae: molecular, empirical, general, structural, displayed, skeletal. CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ for non-cyclic alkanes; each ring or C=C removes 2 H.
Functional groups and name endings: -ane, -ene, halo-, -ol, -al, -one, -oic acid, -oate, -amine, -nitrile.
Primary/secondary/tertiary: number of C atoms attached to the carbon carrying the functional group.
sp³ tetrahedral 109.5°; sp² trigonal planar 120°; sp linear 180°. A π bond prevents rotation about C=C.
Homolytic fission → free radicals; heterolytic fission → ions.
Nucleophile: electron-pair donor. Electrophile: electron-pair acceptor.
Reaction types: addition, substitution, elimination, hydrolysis, condensation, oxidation, reduction.
Structural isomers: chain, positional, functional group.
Geometrical isomers need a C=C with two different groups on each carbon.
A chiral centre has four different groups; one chiral centre → two optical isomers (non-superimposable mirror images).
Number of stereoisomers = 2ⁿ (n = number of chiral centres plus cis/trans C=C bonds).

practice.a: C₆H₁₄O₂; empirical C₃H₇O; a six-carbon zig-zag with OH at each end.

practice.q: Draw (describe) all the structural isomers of C₄H₉Br and classify each.
Explain why pent-2-ene has cis/trans isomers but pent-1-ene does not.
practice.a: Restricted rotation about C=C in both, but in pent-1-ene one carbon of the C=C carries two identical H atoms.

practice.q: How many stereoisomers does CH₃CH(OH)CH(OH)CH₂CH₃ have? (Assume all are different.)
Classify each reaction: (a) C₂H₄ + H₂O → C₂H₅OH (b) C₂H₅Br + OH⁻ → C₂H₅OH + Br⁻ (c) C₂H₅OH → C₂H₄ + H₂O.

assessment.q: What is the empirical formula of ethanoic acid, CH₃COOH?

assessment.why: Two C atoms on the C–OH carbon.
Two different groups on each C of the C=C.
C2 has H, OH, CH₃, C₂H₅.

assessment.q: Bond angle around an sp² carbon?
Number of structural isomers of C₅H₁₂?
Which type of reaction is ester formation from an acid and an alcohol?
assessment.why: Two molecules join and water is lost.

assessment.q: How many stereoisomers does a molecule with three chiral centres have (maximum)?

assessment_s.q:
Compound P is CH₃CH=CHCH(Br)CH₃.
(a) Give its systematic name. [1]
(b) Explain why P has geometrical isomers. [2]
(c) Identify the chiral centre in P and state how many stereoisomers P has in total. [2]
(d) P reacts with OH⁻ in a substitution reaction. State the role of OH⁻ and the type of bond fission at the C–Br bond. [2]
assessment_s.a:
(a) 4-bromopent-2-ene
(b) restricted rotation about C=C; each C of the C=C carries two different groups (H and CH₃; H and CHBrCH₃)
(c) C4 (bonded to H, Br, CH₃ and CH=CHCH₃); 4 stereoisomers
(d) nucleophile (electron-pair donor); heterolytic

assessment_s.q:
C₄H₈O has several isomers.
(a) Give the structural formulae of an aldehyde and a ketone with this formula, and name them. [2]
(b) State the type of structural isomerism between them. [1]
(c) Give the skeletal description of an isomer that contains a C=C and an OH group and has geometrical isomers. [1]
assessment_s.a:
(a) CH₃CH₂CH₂CHO butanal (or (CH₃)₂CHCHO methylpropanal); CH₃COCH₂CH₃ butanone
(b) functional group isomerism
(c) but-2-en-1-ol, CH₃CH=CHCH₂OH

pp.skill: Molecular and empirical formula from a structure
pp.mis: Not dividing by the common factor
pp.stem: Lactic acid has the structural formula CH₃CH(OH)COOH. What are its molecular and empirical formulae?
pp.exp: Count: 3 C, 6 H (3 + 1 + 1 + 1), 3 O. Dividing by 3 gives CH₂O.

pp.skill: Empirical formula of a compound
pp.mis: Giving the molecular formula
pp.stem: Butane-1,4-diamine is H₂N(CH₂)₄NH₂. What is its empirical formula?
pp.exp: Molecular formula C₄H₁₂N₂ (4 CH₂ = 8 H, plus 2 × NH₂ = 4 H). Divide by 2: C₂H₆N.

pp.skill: Molecular formula of a ring compound
pp.mis: Forgetting that each ring removes two H
pp.stem: Menthol is a cyclohexane ring with an OH group on carbon 1, an isopropyl group, –CH(CH₃)₂, on carbon 2 and a methyl group on carbon 5. What is its molecular formula?
pp.exp: Carbons: 6 (ring) + 3 + 1 = 10. A saturated compound with one ring has formula CₙH₂ₙO: C₁₀H₂₀O. (C₁₀H₂₂O would be non-cyclic.)

pp.skill: Formula and M<sub>r</sub> of an amino acid
pp.mis: Miscounting hydrogens on N and O
pp.stem: Serine is HOCH₂CH(NH₂)COOH. Which row is correct?

pp.skill: Formula and chirality of a drug molecule
pp.mis: Counting the benzene carbons as chiral
pp.stem: Ibuprofen is 2-[4-(2-methylpropyl)phenyl]propanoic acid: a benzene ring carrying –CH₂CH(CH₃)₂ and –CH(CH₃)COOH on opposite carbons. Which statement is correct?
opts: It has one chiral carbon; formula C₁₃H₁₈O₂.
It has two chiral carbons; formula C₁₃H₁₈O₂.
It has one chiral carbon; formula C₁₃H₂₀O₂.
It has no chiral carbon; formula C₁₂H₁₆O₂.
pp.exp: Only the CH carrying CH₃, COOH, H and the ring is chiral; the CH in the isobutyl group has two identical CH₃ groups. Formula C₁₃H₁₈O₂ (M<sub>r</sub> 206).

pp.skill: Classifying alcohols
pp.mis: Counting carbons in the whole molecule
pp.stem: Which row shows a primary, a secondary and a tertiary alcohol, in that order?
pp.exp: Classify by the number of carbons attached to the C bearing OH: one (primary), two (secondary), three (tertiary).

pp.skill: Functional groups possible for a given empirical formula
pp.mis: Forgetting that the molecular formula can be a multiple
pp.stem:
Compound T has empirical formula CH₂O and contains only one functional group. Which functional groups are possible?
1 aldehyde
2 carboxylic acid
3 ester
4 alcohol
pp.exp: HCHO (aldehyde), CH₃COOH (acid) and HCOOCH₃ (ester) all fit (CH₂O)ₙ. A molecule whose only functional group is a single OH (CₙH₂ₙ₊₁OH or a ring alcohol) never has the ratio CH₂O.

pp.skill: A functional group isomer that is chiral
pp.mis: Choosing an isomer that is not chiral
pp.stem: Methoxypropane, CH₃OCH₂CH₂CH₃, is an ether. Y is a functional group isomer of methoxypropane and exists as a pair of optical isomers. What is Y?
pp.exp: Y must be an alcohol C₄H₁₀O. Only butan-2-ol has a carbon with four different groups (H, OH, CH₃, C₂H₅). 2-methoxypropane is still an ether.

pp.skill: Definition of an electrophile
pp.mis: Thinking every electrophile is a positive ion
pp.stem: Which statement is true of every electrophile?
opts: It accepts a pair of electrons.
It donates a lone pair of electrons.
pp.exp: An electrophile is an electron-pair acceptor. Many are neutral but polarised (Br₂ near a C=C, the δ+ H in HBr).

pp.skill: Recognising free radicals
pp.mis: Thinking any ion is a radical
pp.stem:
Which species are free radicals?
1 CH₃•
2 Br•
3 OH⁻
4 NO (nitrogen monoxide)
pp.exp: A free radical has an unpaired electron. NO has 11 valence electrons (odd number), so it is a radical. OH⁻ has all electrons paired.

pp.skill: Homolytic and heterolytic fission
pp.mis: Mixing up the two
pp.stem: Which describes heterolytic fission of the C–Br bond in bromoethane?
opts: Each atom takes one electron, forming two free radicals.
Both electrons go to bromine, forming a carbocation and Br⁻.
Both electrons go to carbon, forming a carbanion and Br⁺.
The bond breaks only in ultraviolet light.
pp.exp: Heterolytic: both electrons go to one atom, usually the more electronegative one. Homolytic fission gives two radicals (often in UV light).

pp.skill: Identifying positional isomers
pp.mis: Confusing chain and positional isomers
pp.stem: Which pair are positional isomers?
pp.exp: Same chain, same functional group, different position. B are chain isomers, C functional group isomers, D stereoisomers.

pp.skill: Choosing a structural isomer
pp.mis: Not checking the molecular formula
pp.stem: Which compound is a structural isomer of hexan-2-one, CH₃CO(CH₂)₃CH₃?
pp.exp: Hexan-2-one is C₆H₁₂O. 3-methylpentan-2-one is also C₆H₁₂O. Pentan-2-one is C₅H₁₀O, hexan-2-ol C₆H₁₄O, cyclohexanone C₆H₁₀O.

pp.skill: Types of structural isomerism among carbonyl compounds
pp.mis: Calling aldehyde/ketone isomers positional
pp.stem: Four isomers of C₅H₁₀O: 1 pentanal; 2 pentan-2-one; 3 3-methylbutanal; 4 pentan-3-one. Which statement is correct?
pp.exp: 1 and 3: same group (aldehyde), different carbon chains. 2 and 4 are positional isomers; 1 and 2 are functional group isomers; 3, (CH₃)₂CHCH₂CHO, has no chiral carbon.

pp.skill: Counting structural isomers of an alkene
pp.mis: Counting cis and trans separately
pp.stem: Considering structural isomers only, how many non-cyclic alkenes have the formula C₅H₁₀?
pp.exp: pent-1-ene, pent-2-ene, 2-methylbut-1-ene, 3-methylbut-1-ene, 2-methylbut-2-ene. (Cis and trans pent-2-ene are stereoisomers, not separate structural isomers.)

pp.skill: Counting secondary halogenoalkanes
pp.mis: Counting a primary isomer as secondary
pp.stem: Considering structural isomers only, how many compounds with formula C₅H₁₁Cl are secondary halogenoalkanes?
pp.exp: 2-chloropentane, 3-chloropentane and 2-chloro-3-methylbutane. (Four are primary and one, 2-chloro-2-methylbutane, is tertiary.)

pp.skill: Counting alcohols of each type
pp.mis: Missing branched isomers
pp.stem: Considering structural isomers only, how many primary, secondary and tertiary alcohols have the formula C₄H₁₀O?
pp.exp: Primary: butan-1-ol, 2-methylpropan-1-ol. Secondary: butan-2-ol. Tertiary: 2-methylpropan-2-ol.

pp.skill: Counting dihalogenoalkane isomers
pp.mis: Missing the two halogens on one carbon
pp.stem: Considering structural isomers only, how many isomers have the formula C₃H₆Cl₂?
pp.exp: 1,1-, 1,2-, 1,3- and 2,2-dichloropropane.

pp.skill: Counting sp² carbon atoms
pp.mis: Forgetting the carbonyl carbon
pp.stem: How many carbon atoms in propenal, CH₂=CH–CHO, are sp² hybridised?
pp.exp: Both C=C carbons and the C=O carbon have three regions of electron density: all three are sp² (trigonal planar, 120°).

pp.skill: Which alkene shows cis/trans isomerism
pp.mis: Ignoring two identical groups on one carbon
pp.stem: Which alkene shows geometrical (cis/trans) isomerism?
pp.exp: Each C of the C=C must carry two different groups. Hex-3-ene: H and C₂H₅ on each. Hex-1-ene has =CH₂; the others have two CH₃ on one carbon.

pp.skill: Which compound has stereoisomers
pp.mis: Looking for a double bond only
pp.stem: Which compound exhibits stereoisomerism?
pp.exp: ClCH=CHCl has cis and trans forms (restricted rotation, two different groups on each C). The others have free rotation or identical groups, and no chiral centre.

pp.skill: Naming the isomerism of two related acids
pp.mis: Calling it positional
pp.stem: Maleic acid and fumaric acid are both HOOC–CH=CH–COOH. In maleic acid the two COOH groups are on the same side of the C=C; in fumaric acid, opposite sides. What type of isomerism is this?
pp.exp: Same structure, different spatial arrangement about a C=C that cannot rotate: cis (maleic) and trans (fumaric).

pp.skill: Counting structural and geometrical isomers
pp.mis: Missing the cis/trans pair
pp.stem: Including stereoisomers, how many non-cyclic isomers have the formula C₃H₅Cl?
pp.exp: cis- and trans-1-chloroprop-1-ene, 2-chloropropene, 3-chloropropene.

pp.skill: Shape and isomerism of a ring alkene
pp.mis: Assuming all ring carbons are planar
pp.stem: Student X says that all six carbon atoms of cyclohexene lie in one plane. Student Y says that cyclohexene shows cis/trans isomerism at its C=C bond. Who is correct?
pp.exp: The four sp³ CH₂ carbons are tetrahedral, so the ring is puckered. Each C=C carbon carries H and a ring carbon, but the ring forces the cis arrangement: no separate trans isomer exists.

pp.skill: Smallest chiral molecule of a homologous series
pp.mis: Not checking for four different groups
pp.stem: Alcohols CₙH₂ₙ₊₁OH are written out for n = 1, 2, 3 … The first one in the series that can exist as a pair of optical isomers has how many carbons?
pp.exp: Butan-2-ol, CH₃CH(OH)CH₂CH₃: the C2 carries H, OH, CH₃ and C₂H₅. Propan-2-ol has two CH₃ groups.

pp.skill: Spotting chiral carbons in a sugar
pp.mis: Counting CH₂OH or CHO carbons
pp.stem: The open-chain form of ribose is HOCH₂–CH(OH)–CH(OH)–CH(OH)–CHO. X is the CHO carbon, Y is the carbon next to it, Z is the CH₂OH carbon. Which are chiral centres?
pp.exp: Only carbons with four different groups are chiral: the three CH(OH) carbons. X (C=O) has three groups; Z has two H atoms.

pp.skill: Counting chiral centres in a ring compound
pp.mis: Missing ring carbons
pp.stem: How many chiral centres are in a menthol molecule (cyclohexane ring with OH on C1, –CH(CH₃)₂ on C2 and CH₃ on C5)?
pp.exp: C1 (OH), C2 (isopropyl) and C5 (methyl) each have four different groups, because the two ring paths from them differ. The isopropyl CH has two identical CH₃.

pp.skill: Chiral centres in an amino acid
pp.mis: Counting the COOH carbon
pp.stem: How many chiral centres are in threonine, CH₃CH(OH)CH(NH₂)COOH?
pp.exp: The CH(OH) carbon (H, OH, CH₃, rest) and the CH(NH₂) carbon (H, NH₂, COOH, rest) are both chiral.

pp.skill: Chiral centres in a diol
pp.mis: Missing the central carbon
pp.stem: How many chiral centres are in 3-methylhexane-2,4-diol, CH₃CH(OH)CH(CH₃)CH(OH)CH₂CH₃?
pp.exp: C2 and C4 carry OH, H and two different chains. C3 carries H, CH₃, CH(OH)CH₃ and CH(OH)CH₂CH₃, which are different, so it is chiral too.

pp.skill: A molecule with no chiral centre
pp.mis: Assuming a crowded carbon must be chiral
pp.stem: How many chiral centres are in citric acid, HOOC–CH₂–C(OH)(COOH)–CH₂–COOH?
pp.exp: The central carbon carries OH, COOH and two identical CH₂COOH groups, so it is not chiral.

pp.skill: Stereoisomers from a C=C and a chiral centre
pp.mis: Adding instead of multiplying
pp.stem: How many stereoisomers are there of hex-4-en-3-ol, CH₃CH=CHCH(OH)CH₂CH₃?
pp.exp: The C=C gives cis and trans; the CH(OH) is a chiral centre (two forms). 2 × 2 = 4.

pp.skill: Comparing numbers of stereoisomers
pp.mis: Ignoring a chiral centre next to the double bond
pp.stem: Which compound has the greatest number of stereoisomers?
pp.exp: 4-methylhex-2-ene, CH₃CH=CHCH(CH₃)CH₂CH₃: cis/trans and a chiral C4 → 4. A and B: cis/trans only (2). C: chiral only (2).

pp.skill: Stereoisomers with two chiral centres and a C=C
pp.mis: Counting only the chiral centres
pp.stem: How many stereoisomers have the structural formula CH₃CH=CHCH(OH)CH(CH₃)COOH?
pp.exp: One C=C with two different groups on each carbon (×2) and two chiral centres (×2 × 2): 2³ = 8.

pp.skill: Stereoisomers of an unsaturated ketone
pp.mis: Missing the chiral centre beside the carbonyl
pp.stem: Including the compound itself, how many stereoisomers have the structure CH₃CH=CHCOCH(CH₃)CH₂CH₃?
pp.exp: The C=C (cis/trans) and the CH(CH₃) carbon (chiral: H, CH₃, C₂H₅, COCH=CHCH₃) give 2 × 2 = 4.

pp.skill: Classifying, and the origin of geometrical isomerism
pp.stem: This question is about the isomers of C₄H₈ and C₄H₉Cl.

parts.q: Explain why 2-chloro-2-methylpropane is a tertiary halogenoalkane.
ms: the carbon bonded to Cl is attached to three other carbon atoms

parts.q: Give the structural formula and systematic name of a C₄H₈ alkene that has geometrical isomers.
State and explain the origin of geometrical isomerism in alkenes.
ms: restricted rotation about the C=C bond (the π bond prevents rotation)
each carbon of the C=C has two different groups attached

parts.q: Name a structural isomer of but-2-ene that does not show geometrical isomerism and say why.
ms: but-1-ene (or methylpropene): one C of the C=C has two identical groups (two H, or two CH₃)

pp.skill: Drawing optical isomers and counting stereoisomers
pp.stem: 2-bromobutane, CH₃CHBrCH₂CH₃, exists as a pair of optical isomers.

parts.q: Define chiral centre and identify it in 2-bromobutane.
ms: a carbon atom bonded to four different atoms or groups
C2 (bonded to H, Br, CH₃ and C₂H₅)

parts.q: Describe how to draw the two optical isomers in three dimensions.
ms: tetrahedral arrangement with wedge/dash bonds around C2
the two drawn as non-superimposable mirror images

parts.q: How many stereoisomers does pent-3-en-2-ol, CH₃CH=CHCH(OH)CH₃, have? Explain.
ms: cis/trans about C=C (2) × two optical forms at the chiral C2 (2)
